\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{துக்கம்} (tukkam)}{துக்கம் (tukkam)}]{\ta{துக்கம்} (tukkam) — grief; mourning}

\label{lesson:TA-C463-tukkam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for disgust, then the Tamil for to grimace.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{துக்கம்}}
\textbf{\ta{துக்கம்}} — \emph{tukkam} — \textquotedblleft{}grief; mourning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{நண்பன்} \ta{ஊரை} \ta{விட்டுப்} \ta{போனதால்} \ta{எனக்குத்} \ta{துக்கமாக} \ta{இருந்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{naṇpaṉ ūrai viṭṭup pōṉatāl eṉakkut tukkamāka iruntatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I was sad because my friend left town.
\end{quote}

A house in mourning is a \ta{துக்க} \ta{வீடு}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{துக்கம்}} (\emph{tukkam}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{duḥkha}, \textquotedblleft{}difficulty, pain\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6375); Tamil writes the cluster as \ta{க்க}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tukkam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tukkam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naṇpaṉ ūrai viṭṭup pōṉatāl eṉakkut tukkamāka iruntatu.} — I was sad because my friend left town.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for disgust, then the Tamil for to grimace, then say \emph{tukkam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{துக்கம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Grief; mourning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{வேதனை} (vētaṉai)}{வேதனை (vētaṉai)}]{\ta{வேதனை} (vētaṉai) — torment; anguish}

\label{lesson:TA-C463-vetanai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to grimace, then the Tamil for grief.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{வேதனை}}
\textbf{\ta{வேதனை}} — \emph{vētaṉai} — \textquotedblleft{}torment; anguish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{காயத்தின்} \ta{வலி} \ta{அவருக்கு} \ta{வேதனை} \ta{தந்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāyattiṉ vali avarukku vētaṉai tantatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The pain of the wound tormented him.
\end{quote}

Pain of body or of mind: \ta{மன} \ta{வேதனை}, anguish.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{வேதனை}} (\emph{vētaṉai}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{vēdanā}, \textquotedblleft{}feeling; pain\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12106).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vētaṉai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vētaṉai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāyattiṉ vali avarukku vētaṉai tantatu.} — The pain of the wound tormented him.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to grimace, then the Tamil for grief, then say \emph{vētaṉai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{வேதனை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Torment; anguish\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{துன்பம்} (tuṉpam)}{துன்பம் (tuṉpam)}]{\ta{துன்பம்} (tuṉpam) — suffering; hardship}

\label{lesson:TA-C463-tunpam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for grief, then the Tamil for torment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{துன்பம்}}
\textbf{\ta{துன்பம்}} — \emph{tuṉpam} — \textquotedblleft{}suffering; hardship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{வெள்ளத்தால்} \ta{அந்தக்} \ta{கிராம} \ta{மக்கள்} \ta{துன்பப்பட்டார்கள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{veḷḷattāl antak kirāma makkaḷ tuṉpappaṭṭārkaḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because of the flood the people of that village suffered.
\end{quote}

\ta{துன்பப்படு}, to suffer. \ta{இன்பம்}, delight, is its opposite.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{துன்பம்}} (\emph{tuṉpam}) is native Dravidian (DEDR 3372), a word for affliction, sorrow and want.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuṉpam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuṉpam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{veḷḷattāl antak kirāma makkaḷ tuṉpappaṭṭārkaḷ.} — Because of the flood the people of that village suffered.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for grief, then the Tamil for torment, then say \emph{tuṉpam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{துன்பம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Suffering; hardship\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{வெறுமை} (veṟumai)}{வெறுமை (veṟumai)}]{\ta{வெறுமை} (veṟumai) — emptiness}

\label{lesson:TA-C463-verumai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for torment, then the Tamil for suffering.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{வெறுமை}}
\textbf{\ta{வெறுமை}} — \emph{veṟumai} — \textquotedblleft{}emptiness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{குழந்தைகள்} \ta{வெளிநாட்டுக்குப்} \ta{போன} \ta{பிறகு} \ta{வீடு} \ta{வெறுமையாக} \ta{இருந்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kuḻantaikaḷ veḷināṭṭukkup pōṉa piṟaku vīṭu veṟumaiyāka iruntatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the children went abroad the house felt empty.
\end{quote}

From \ta{வெறு} \textquotedblleft{}empty\textquotedblright{} (\ta{வெறும்} \ta{கை}, an empty hand), not from \ta{வெறு} \textquotedblleft{}to hate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{வெறுமை}} (\emph{veṟumai}) is native Dravidian (DEDR 5513), the noun of \ta{வெறு} \emph{veṟu}, \textquotedblleft{}empty\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{veṟumai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{veṟumai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuḻantaikaḷ veḷināṭṭukkup pōṉa piṟaku vīṭu veṟumaiyāka iruntatu.} — After the children went abroad the house felt empty.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for torment, then the Tamil for suffering, then say \emph{veṟumai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{வெறுமை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Emptiness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{இரங்கல்} (iraṅkal)}{இரங்கல் (iraṅkal)}]{\ta{இரங்கல்} (iraṅkal) — condolence}

\label{lesson:TA-C463-irankal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for suffering, then the Tamil for emptiness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{இரங்கல்}}
\textbf{\ta{இரங்கல்}} — \emph{iraṅkal} — \textquotedblleft{}condolence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அந்தக்} \ta{குடும்பத்துக்கு} \ta{நாங்கள்} \ta{இரங்கல்} \ta{தெரிவித்தோம்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{antak kuṭumpattukku nāṅkaḷ iraṅkal terivittōm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We offered our condolences to that family.
\end{quote}

\ta{இரங்கல்} \ta{கூட்டம்}, a memorial meeting.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{இரங்கல்}} (\emph{iraṅkal}) is native Dravidian, a noun from \ta{இரங்கு} \emph{iraṅku}, \textquotedblleft{}to feel pity, to be grieved\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 473).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iraṅkal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iraṅkal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antak kuṭumpattukku nāṅkaḷ iraṅkal terivittōm.} — We offered our condolences to that family.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for suffering, then the Tamil for emptiness, then say \emph{iraṅkal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{இரங்கல்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Condolence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
